newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Le Pensec says farm aid must be fair.
newsitem.headline: France's Le Pensec says farm aid must be fair.

text.p: France's new farm minister Louis Le Pensec on Thursday set the tone of his administration when he said he favoured a fairer distribution of subsidies paid to European Union farmers.
Le Pensec, who described himself as "the son of a farm labourer" in rural Britanny, also said the interests of large market-oriented producers must be reconciled with those of smaller farmers.
"I think the idea that must prevail is that of a balance between various forms of agriculture and of a fairness in public supports," Le Pensec said at a handover ceremony at the farm ministry.
Le Pensec was appointed on Wednesday to replace centre-right coalition minister Philippe Vasseur.
"I do not support the idea of a separation between two forms of agriculture - one that is market-oriented and another that focuses on rural development or natural resources preservation," he said.
Le Pensec was echoing ideas floated by Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin to impose a ceiling on EU compensatory payments in order to obtain a fair distribution among farmers.
This may however not play well with large grain producers in northern France who receive advantages for keeping crop land idle and have been accused of being oversubsidised,
